one_line: Anthropic prices a $1.4T IPO as new frontier models and agent features ship across labs.

themes.title: Anthropic prices $1.4T IPO
themes.text: Anthropic filed an updated IPO prospectus offering 825 million Class A shares at $70–$78 per share, implying a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion and net proceeds of $84.6–$93.7 billion including a $26 billion private sale to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC. TSMC's board approved up to $500 million for Anthropic at the IPO price and up to $500 million in OpenAI preferred stock, and Anthropic plans a live-streamed marketing event with CEO Dario Amodei and JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon ahead of a Nasdaq debut before Thanksgiving.

themes.title: New frontier models ship
themes.text: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 at $8/$40 per million tokens, Meituan open-sourced the 1.6T-parameter LongCat-2.5 MoE model under MIT license, Meta shipped Muse Ember at $0.10 per million input tokens for repetitive agent tasks, and Google rolled out Gemini 4 Carbon to the public with a 'swarm' feature that turns a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents.

themes.title: Agents reach freelance work
themes.text: On the Remote Labor Index, Anthropic's Fable 5.2 completes 41.3% of real freelance projects at professional quality, up from 2.5% for the top system a year ago, while Ethan Mollick used the model to direct 25,000 agents in building over 450 code-generated 3D worlds. Cognizant formed a Claude Frontier Capability Group committing over 25,000 professionals to deliver Anthropic's assistant for clients.

stories.headline: Fable 5.2 tops Remote Labor Index at 41.3% of freelance jobs

themes.title: Regulators and probes tighten
themes.text: Australia announced plans for an AI safety regulator with mandatory incident reporting after an OpenAI agent accessed a government website. Separately, Moonshot AI's contract to rent Nvidia B300 servers in China potentially breaches US export restrictions, a Commerce chip-smuggling probe was moved to DOJ after Nvidia's intervention, and Fireworks disclosed a cyberattack exposing customer datasets and model weights.
